Afsar vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:146292
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 29642 of 2023

Applicant :- Afsar
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Chandra Prakash Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.

1. Heard Sri C.P.Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Dr. S.B.Maurya, learned Aga-I, for the
State.

2.  The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.61 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376, 368 and 506 IPC, Police Station Rabupura, District Gautam Budh Nagar during pendency of the trial.
3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and co-accused Firoz and according to the FIR, applicant enticed away the minor daughter of the informant aged about 16 years.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that entire allegation against the applicant is totally false and actually prosecutrix is a major girl aged about 20 years and she according to her own wish had gone along with applicant as applicant and prosecutrix loved each other but when she was recovered then under the pressure of her parents she started making allegation of rape against the applicant.

1 5.

He further submits that even from her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. it appears that victim was consenting party as she had gone along with applicant upto Ajmer but in between she did not raise any alarm.
6. He next submits that as per the certificate issued by CMO concerned, victim was around 26 years old.
He next submits that victim is illiterate girl and therefore there is no school record with regard to her age.
7. He next submits that applicant is not having any previous criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 22.3.2023, i.e., for the last about more than three months.
8. Per contra, learned AGA although opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that victim is a major girl aged about 20 years.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. Although, victim in her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. made allegation of rape against the applicant but she is major girl aged about 22 years and the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant that even from her both the statements recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. it can not be said that she was not consenting part, cannot be ruled out as admittedly prosecutrix had gone along with applicant upto Ajmer but she did not raise any alarm.
11.

Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
12. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

13. Let the applicant-Afsar be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless her personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
14. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
